_comment: First mutation baseline (v0.28.6). Scope is THREE files only. Scope and exclusions are recorded in _mutateNote below, NOT in docs/mutation-baseline.md — that file records the RUN: the score, all 209 classified survivors, the guard, and the cost. This pointer used to send readers there for what was excluded and why. That file contains no occurrence of the word snapshots and documents no exclusion, so the reference was false from the day it was written; corrected v0.28.15. Run via `npm run mutate`, never `npx stryker` directly: the wrapper deletes the previous report before running, because a run that fails to start emits no survivors and no score, which is indistinguishable from a perfect result. This is a BASELINE, not a gate — `npm run mutate` is deliberately NOT a shipgate step and must not be wired into shipgate.config.json.
_vitestNote: No scoped vitest config. The full suite runs in ~9s and coverageAnalysis perTest already restricts execution to covering tests. A scoped config would also reintroduce the transitive-import-derivation hazard that a narrowed `include` creates; not having one removes it rather than mitigating it.
_tsconfigNote: The plain tsconfig, not a stryker-specific one. v0.28.2 made `tsc --noEmit` clean INCLUDING test files, so there is nothing for a side-step config to work around here.
_mutateNote: 546 branches, all >=85% branch coverage. Selected because the canonical Firestore rules carry 44 keys().hasOnly() field allowlists and ZERO is-string / size() / matches() value checks — so a mutant corrupting a date validator or a sanitiser has no independent expression anywhere in the system. Excluded, and the exclusions STAND — nothing here implies a re-scoping, which is a separate decision. snapshots.ts failed the ~70% branch gate at 58.49% br; v0.28.14 then deleted five dead exports from it and it now measures 79.48% br (31/39), clearing that gate but not the >=85% the three selected files meet. local-storage-driver.ts belongs with the 100%-branch small utilities below rather than here: it measures 6/6 = 100% br, and neither it nor its test has changed since v12.6, so the 33.33% br once attributed to it never described it. 33.33% was snapshots.ts's own FUNCTION coverage (4/12) — the cell immediately right of its 58.49% branch cell in the same reporter row, i.e. two figures from one row attributed to two files. Corrected v0.28.15; six zero-branch constant/barrel files have nothing to mutate; the 100%-branch small utilities would return near-total kill and little information; the three Firebase-importing storage files are not pure logic.
_reportersNote: ⚠️ Passing --reporters on the CLI REPLACES this array, silently dropping `json` and with it the report file that mutation-guard.mjs and every future comparison depend on. If a run needs a different reporter set, change it here.
_jsonReporterNote: ⚠️ Load-bearing, with no compile-time link to its consumer: scripts/mutation-guard.mjs:31 hard-codes path.resolve('reports/mutation/mutation.json'). Changing either side alone breaks the guard silently — it would report 'no report written' for a run that succeeded.
_excludedMutationsNote: None, deliberately. The suite disagrees here — the Vite siblings exclude StringLiteral/ObjectLiteral, MyScrumBudget excludes nothing. A FIRST baseline should see the full mutant population: excluding shrinks the denominator before anyone knows what is in it. If StringLiteral proves to be a large EQUIV cluster of unasserted error messages, that is a finding to record and a reason to exclude in a later COMPARISON run.
_thresholdsComment: No `break` threshold. A baseline is a measurement, not a gate; it must not be able to fail a release. Wiring one in is a separate, deliberate decision, and §8 of this item's brief is explicit that a recorded baseline with classified survivors is the deliverable — not a score target.
